definition: Preponderance means a superiority in number, weight, or importance — the greater part or share of something.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word preponderance. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know preponderance should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: In the civil trial, the jury needed only a preponderance of the physical evidence to side with the plaintiff.
A majority is simply more than half; a preponderance suggests a weightier, more decisive share that clearly outweighs the rest.
Dominance is stronger than preponderance — not just outweighing everything else, but actively controlling it.

Predominance is the condition of being the most numerous or influential — the predominance of oaks in a forest. It names the state itself, not the people or votes that hold it. Preponderance likewise names superior weight or share, but it is the standard term of formal analysis, especially 'a preponderance of the evidence.'

The bulk of something is its main or largest part, with a physical, mass-like feel — the bulk of the cargo, the bulk of the work. Preponderance adds judgment to the arithmetic: the greater share outweighs the rest and tips a decision, as when a preponderance of the evidence decides a civil case.

The lion's share is the informal term for the biggest cut of something being divided — the lion's share of the credit or the budget. It belongs to casual talk. Preponderance does formal, analytical work: it names the side whose weight or numbers outbalance the rest, at home in courtrooms and reports.

When the asteroid hypothesis was first proposed in 1980, it competed with an older idea: that vast volcanic eruptions had ended the age of dinosaurs.
For a decade the two camps traded findings, and neither could land a decisive blow.
Then the crater was found off the Yucatan coast, its age matching the extinction layer almost exactly.
Volcanism kept its defenders, but the preponderance of the evidence had shifted: iridium layers, shocked quartz, and now a crater of the right age all sat on one side of the scale.
Most geologists concluded, not that the volcano camp had been refuted outright, but that the weight of findings tipped clearly the other way.
